questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a compound Boolean statement built from two given propositions.
questions.question: Let \(P\): "11 is divisible by 2" and \(Q\): "8 is an odd number". Given these facts, which of the following compound statements is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Since "11 is divisible by 2" is False, \(P = \text{False}\); since "8 is an odd number" is False, \(Q = \text{False}\). Evaluating \(P \lor \neg Q\) with these values gives TRUE, while the other listed expressions evaluate to the opposite truth value.
questions.hint: First determine the truth value of each atomic proposition from the given facts, then substitute those values into each expression one operator at a time, applying NOT before AND before OR.

questions.learningObjective: Determine what can validly be inferred about one part of a true conditional statement, given information about the other part.
questions.question: Suppose \(X \rightarrow Y\) is true, and \(Y\) is true. What can we conclude about \(X\)?

options.label: B

options.text: No — neither direction of implication holds between these two statements.

options.text: It depends on which proposition is assumed true first.
